According to reports, Apple has cut iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max orders due to "weak demand." A recent report by Nikkei Asia indicates that Apple has informed specific suppliers to reduce component production for the two models, as the price hike is said to have "dampened consumer demand."

Price hike reportedly hits iPhone 18 Pro demand

Citing "multiple informed sources," the report states that Apple "has turned cautious since early September." Two of the sources said component orders in October were cut by "at least 15%" compared to Apple's original requests.

Another supply chain manager, who spoke anonymously to Nikkei Asia, said demand was "not as strong as when new models used to launch together," referring of course to the fact that Apple will not release the base iPhone 18 until next spring. Suppliers, however, say this alone is not enough to explain the weak demand.

The most popular comment was posted by BlueLamp

To be honest, these companies have successfully convinced everyone that spending £1,000 to £2,000 on a phone that only makes and receives calls is the way to go. They keep raising prices and profit margins, yet consumers happily pay up. Paying so much for a phone has become the new norm, and we are all fools, myself included. Every year it's the same completely meaningless spec upgrades that change nothing, yet we keep buying phones with no real improvements. I just don't know when people will finally have enough and stick with the phones they've been using for five or six years.

Another source added that the "iPhone Duo" is also expected to meet the same fate after launch, referring to potential production cuts.

Apple priced the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max $100 higher than the previous generation. The report says that although demand has taken a hit, this price increase also means the decline in demand will not "immediately translate into a drop in Apple's revenue."

Apple will release its fiscal year 2026 fourth-quarter results on Monday, November 6, which will offer a glimpse into demand for the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max during their first few weeks on the market.
